The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.

4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AK-1638.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act is pleaded.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of insured vehicle is denied by this respondent.
Per contra it is alleged that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the petitioner himself as he was sustained injuries due to self fall from two wheeler.
Further the petitioner colluded with police falsely implicated the insured vehicle in order to get unlawful gain from this respondent.
Further the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the Bolero vehicle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.15,00,000/- together.
The case of the petitioner lies an narrow compass as to claiming of compensation amount for injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident.
Before dwelling into analyzing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have the birds eye of the case of petitioner in a nutshell.

11. In support of case of petitioner himself stepped into the witness box & filed his affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination- in-chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P13 documents.
The petitioner also got examined the doctor who was assessed the disability is examined as PW.2 and through him Ex.P.14 & 15 were marked.
In order to falsify the case of the petitioner and to substantiate the defense of the respondent no.2, their counsel had cross-examined PW1 & 2 at length.
12. Repelling to the contentions urged by the petitioner, the respondent No.2 had attacked the case of the petitioner on various prisms known to fact and law.
The sole defence of respondent No.2 is that accident happened because of the negligence on the part of petitioner himself and there is no negligence on the part of insured vehicle driver.
In support of these contentions the respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.
13. This issue revolves round the sphere and ambit as to the alleged rash and negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other matter in issue.
14. Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty: For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.

15. Now let me unfurl each of the contention urged by the rival parties in the beacon of light of documentary and oral evidence placed on record.
The only dispute arise for consideration is with regard alleged rash and negligent act of driver of the Bolero vehicle.
16. It is trite law that the rash and negligence has to proved as a fact-in-issue.
In the instant case on hand the petitioner in order to prove rash and negligence on the part of the Bolero vehicle driver he has produced Ex.P.1 to 6 documents being the police documents.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, the Ex.P.1 FIR has its germane in Ex.P.2 Complaint.

According to the version of the petitioner the accident had happened on 23.09.2020 at about 7.30 p.m and the criminal law was set into motion on 24.09.2020 at about 11.00 p.m there is absolutely no delay in setting criminal law into motion.
17. The main documents on which the petitioner reliance in order to show the negligence in Ex.P.3 being the spot mahazar.

On careful perusal of the spot mahazar it reflects the driver of the Bolero vehicle had drove the vehicle from Exide gate towards Tyvakanahalli gate in a rash and negligent manner and the driver of the vehicle coming opposite side and caused accident.
This document itself speaks in volume that there is a rash and negligent act by the Bolero vehicle driver.

Even the contents of the Ex.P.3 is fortified by the Ex.P.4 being IMV Report of both vehicles, wherein scratch mark found on front right side bumper of KA-05-AK-1638 and further the head light mask, scratch mark found on the left side crash guard, left side foot rest damaged to the vehicle bearing No.KA-51-HE -5291.
If the driver of the Bolero vehicle is driving the same in a normal speed then he could have certainly avoided accident.
Further more Ex.P.4 IMV Report discloses that both the vehicles are damaged in the front.
When such is the case it can be easily gathered that, it is on head on collusion.
From material placed on record it is clearly emanating that the accident happened because of shear negligence on the part of the Bolero vehicle driver.

Even the chargesheet as per Ex.P.6 is also filed as against the Bolero vehicle driver for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
18.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the Milu Jena vs Shree Raksha Construction on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140476155/

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the driver of the Bolero vehicle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the Bolero vehicle and he was charge sheeted.
19. Though PW.1 was cross examined at length by respondent No.2 counsel but nothing fatal was elicited so as to distrust the petitioner's version in his chief-examination.
Even the chargesheet as per Ex.P.6 is also filed as against the driver of the Bolero vehicle.
When such the case absolutely there is no impediment in considering the version of the petitioner herein.
The petitioner has successfully demonstrated there is a negligence on the part of the Bolero vehicle driver.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Bolero vehicle.
On assessing entire evidence the light of oral and documentary proof, the preponderance of probability tilts infavour of petitioner herein.

Hence,
this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
20. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already held herein above, the petitioner proved that he has sustained injuries in RTA which is caused by the vehicle belonging to respondent No.1 and insured with the respondent no.2.
Hence the petitioner is entitle for compensation.
This Court has already held Issue No.1 in the affirmative which makes it more than obvious that the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

Needless to state the quantum of compensation which is awarded has to be proportionate to the nature of the injuries & the compensation has to be awarded by keeping in mind the pecuniary damages and non-pecuniary damages suffered by the injured-claimant.
By pecuniary damages this Court is referring to the actual loss sustained by the petitioner, which can be determined in terms of money, by taking into account the oral or documentary evidence.

Whereas for non-pecuniary damages this Court is referring to the losses that the claimant has though suffered, but will not be able to prove for the reason that it can neither be calculated in terms of the money nor can it be proved leading documentary evidence.
Perhaps the non-pecuniary damages can be figured out by looking into the facts of each case by taking into account the nature of injuries and the aftermath.

It is required to be reminded to oneself that compensation in a case arising out of injury can never be granted on mathematical precision and invariably a good amount of guesswork is involved while determining the compensation in such cases.
21.

Perhaps unlike in a fatal case, in a case involving bodily injury the victim is left to suffer throughout his life; and hence it becomes the bounden duty of the tribunal to award compensation to a victim of permanent disability so as to bring in sustainability and also to ensure that victim is not pushed to poverty.
22. As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : Left comminuted fracture patella and left lateral malleolus fracture.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
The 2- Discharge summaries as per Ex.P.7 of Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient.
On perusal of Sparsh Hospital discharge summary it discloses that he was admitted from 23.09.2020 to 26.09.2020 and from 17.07.2022 to 19.07.2022 (4+3=7 days in total).

During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of :

Conservative management for left lateral malleolus undisplaced fracture and left patella tension band wiring removal was done under spinal anaesthesia.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
23. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
It is the specific case of the petitioner that, owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Nagaraj. B.N as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained total residual physical disability of 40% to the left lower limb and 13% disability to the whole body.
It is elicited during the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that the fractures of like nature will get united within a span of 4 months.
He further admitted that in case of regular usage of limb the muscle power will be improved.
Further it is to be seen whether the aforesaid disability impairs the avocation of the petitioner.
As per the averments made in his evidence affidavit, at the time of accident the petitioner was working as a Technician at M/s Exide Factory and drawing monthly salary of Rs.69,000/- p.m.

In order to substantiate the said fact the petitioner has produced the Ex.P.8 being salary slip for the months of January-2020 to August-2020 and Ex.P.9 being the account statement from 07.01.2020 to 20.01.2021.

On perusal of the same it reflect that he had received total salary in the said months for a sum of Rs.25,613/-, 12,570/-, 17,946/-, 22,350/-, 22,350/- 8169/-, 16240/- and Rs.29,616/-
respectively.
He further deposed that after the accident his services has been terminated and lost his earnings.
During the course of cross-examination he categorically admitted that : "From past 20 days I was working in Exide company.
Now after the accident I am not working there.
I have not resigned the said company and even they have not terminated me.
I can get examine the author of Ex.P.8.
It is true to suggest that my PF is still in existence".
But in order to substantiate the said fact the author of the document is not examined before the court.
Further the salary slips as per Ex.P8 is substantiated by the account statement as per Ex.P9.
Ex . P.8
being salary slips has reference in Ex.P.9 Account statement of the petitioner.
Ex.P.9 Account statement is of 01.01.2020 to 31.01.2021.
It is the specific case of the Respondent No.2 that petitioner has continued his service in Exide company.
It is relevant to note that the account statement and salary slips was produced before the court on 10.01.2024.
The petitioner willfully withheld the account statement after 31.01.2021.
The petitioner has only taken the account statement for the period from 01.01.2020 to 31.01.2021.

Further more on careful perusal of Ex.P.9 Account statement this court can also finds reference of crediting of salary to the account to the petitioner from the Exide company even in the month of January-2021 to the tune of Rs.6,205/- and Rs.4,791/-.
This categorical reveals that the petitioner has still continued his service.

No doubt it is stoutly denied by the petitioner during the course of cross examination that he has left the job at the time as discussed supra that the company has not terminated him and he has also not resigned the company.

Further more it is also admitted by the PW.1 he can produce the bank statement and he examine the employer of the said company,
but for the reasons best known to him, he has not produced the said document or not examined the author.
This factum clearly goes to that the petitioner has continued his service.
Added more the petitioner has not submitted any documents with regard to his pf or ESI settlement claims.
If at all the petitioner has left the job, than his PF might have been settled.

sentences.text: That is to say as the actual financial loss arising out of physical disability is not made out by the claimant, he is not entitled for compensation towards 'loss of future income'.
25. Though PW.1 deposed in his evidence affidavit that due to the injuries sustained in the accident he has lost the future income / earning, but he has not produced any iota of documents.
Non-production of the any documents in this regard results in drawing of an inference that he has not suffered any financial loss during the period of his treatment.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
26.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 7 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied him to the hospital to take his care by leaving their duties.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day and a sum of Rs.10,500/- (1,500 X 7) is awarded under this head.
27. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
The documents discloses that petitioner had sustained injury to Left comminuted fracture patella and left lateral malleolus fracture.
Having regard to the fractures suffered by the petitioner to weight bearing bones and such other attending circumstances.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.80,000/- under this head.
28. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P10, the petitioner has spent Rs.17,609/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.17,609/- which is rounded off to Rs.17,600/- towards medical expenses.
29. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.60,000/- is awarded under this head.
30. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% per annum is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
33. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AK-1638 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
34. ISSUE NO.3 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,68,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
The sole defence of respondent No.2 is that accident happened because of the negligence on the part of petitioner himself and there is no negligence on the part of insured vehicle driver.
It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
The petitioner has successfully demonstrated there is a negligence on the part of the Bolero vehicle driver.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The factum of negligence has to be proved like any other matter in issue.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.

The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.
Even in the instant case the driver of the Bolero vehicle is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the Bolero vehicle and he was charge sheeted.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Bolero vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-AK-1638 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
34. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,68,100/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
